ARC-001-RSCH-v4.1.title: Technology and Service Research: UK Fuel Price Transparency Service

controlFields.Distribution: CMA Digital, DESNZ Policy, GDS Assessors, Delivery Team, Architecture Review Board
controlFields.Environments: Test (sandbox) and Production with separate credentials; test credentials invalid in production and vice versa
controlFields.Rate Limit (Test): 30 RPM per client (burst to 60 RPM), 1 concurrent request
controlFields.Data Freshness: Prices published within 30 minutes of any change (statutory requirement)
controlFields.Sequential Processing: MFT must not send another request until the response for the previous request is received; API returns 429 if violated
controlFields.Changed Prices Only: Price submission requests must only include price changes for each fuel type; unchanged prices must not be resent
controlFields.No Timestamp Manipulation: Fuel types with unchanged prices must not be resent by changing the timestamp (creates unnecessary load; future versions will return an error code)
controlFields.Transaction Polling: Submit price update → poll transaction for status → handle accepted or rejected outcomes
controlFields.GOV.UK One Login Required: Motor fuel traders must authenticate via GOV.UK One Login for price submission credentials
controlFields.Caching: Station data: 1 hour; Price data: 15 minutes; Search results: 5 minutes; use HTTP caching headers when available; implement cache invalidation strategies
controlFields.Security: Never expose secrets in client-side code or public repos; store in env vars or secret managers; use separate credentials per environment and per application; HTTPS only (TLS 1.2+); rotate secrets regularly and immediately if compromise suspected; request minimum scopes (least privilege); do not log secrets or tokens — mask sensitive values; monitor token usage for anomalies (unexpected IPs, request spikes); run OAuth on backend services only — never expose to browsers or mobile apps
controlFields.Error Handling: Check HTTP status codes; exponential backoff retry; 20-second timeout default; translate technical errors into user-friendly language; provide actionable suggestions; offer alternative actions
controlFields.Rate Limiting: Respect limits; 429 returns Retry-After header; up to 3 retries with exponential backoff; test keys must not be used for performance testing or high-volume traffic
controlFields.Request Optimisation: Use appropriate pagination to limit response sizes; request only needed data fields; implement request batching; use compression for large requests; avoid unnecessary requests
controlFields.Testing: Unit test all endpoints; use sandbox environment; mock API responses for consistent testing; test error handling scenarios; validate data parsing; integration test with various data scenarios; verify rate limiting behaviour
controlFields.Monitoring: Track request success/failure rates; monitor response times; alert on unusual usage patterns; track rate limit usage; include request IDs for tracing; implement log rotation and retention policies
controlFields.Data Validation: Check required fields are present; validate data types and formats; handle null/undefined values gracefully; sanitize user inputs before API requests
controlFields.Data Usage: Do not redistribute raw API data; attribute data sources appropriately; respect intellectual property rights; data available under OGL v3.0
controlFields.Compliance: Do not circumvent security; use data responsibly and ethically; respect user privacy and data protection; follow applicable laws and regulations
controlFields.External Dependencies: OS: 50 RPM dev / 600 RPM live; Companies House: strict limits — use cached or mocked responses to avoid quota exhaustion
controlFields.Public API testing: Can test against live or test
